subject: Post-call: CareLane product fit & interop playbook
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@carelane.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Discovery — embed/rerank + streaming requirements

Hi Mina (and Ben),

Thanks for the call earlier today — great overview. I wanted to capture the immediate business pains so we have them in one place before we dive into technical scope: 

- Latency sensitivity: clinicians need sub-300ms turn for short prompts (patient triage snippets).
- Relevance / ranking: our current search returns too many false positives; embeddings + rerank is the highest priority to reduce noise.
- Streaming & partial outputs: we need progressive scoring for UI (rank scores arriving before full text) and deterministic structured outputs for downstream events.
- PII controls / redaction: we cannot send raw PHI off our VPC without explicit redaction plan and auditability.

Goals for PoC:
1) Demonstrate embedding + re-rank improves top-3 precision on triage queries by >=20%
2) Show streaming inference for short prompts with preserved rerank scores arriving incrementally
3) Validate a function-calling pipeline that performs deterministic redaction before any external inference call

Can you confirm whether Redwood can support a hybrid approach (private on-prem adapter for redaction + hosted inference for rerank) or if we should plan for a Private deployment end-to-end? Also, Ben — happy to share an example query set; I'll attach a short sample.

Next steps we discussed on the call: generate a PoC scope doc, proposed timeline, and a short security checklist.

Thanks,
Samira
Director of Product
CareLane Health

Attachments: sample-queries.csv

Samira — thanks for the clear recap and for the sample queries. Recapping the call and pulling out concrete asks so we can align scope: 

Summary of pain & priority:
- Primary pain: low precision on triage search; urgent business metric = clinician time saved (top-3 precision lift is primary success metric).
- Non-negotiable: deterministic PII redaction and audit logs before any external inference.
- UX need: progressive ranking information (partial/streaming scores) to update the UI as results arrive.

Redwood fit & recommended approach (high level):
- Embeddings + server-side reranker: reasonable default. We'll recommend a candidate model family we’ve validated for medical note semantics.
- Streaming + incremental scores: supported via our streaming API; we can emit per-candidate scores as they complete and the UI can merge incremental deltas. This will require small SDK adaptation (client-side streaming consumer).
- Function calling for redaction: recommend an on-prem redaction step that runs deterministic transformations (structured rules + small local model) before any tokens leave your VPC. Redwood Private or a hybrid private adapter both feasible.

Technical asks from Redwood to CareLane (to scope PoC):
- Provide 200–500 labeled queries with expected top-3 results (sample looks good).
- Share a minimal data model for PHI fields you expect to redact and any required audit schema.
- Confirm preferred environment: hybrid (on-prem redactor + hosted rerank) OR full Private deployment.

Proposed PoC deliverables & timeline (tentative):
- Week 0: finalize scope & security checklist (this week)
- Week 1–2: infra & SDK stub changes (streaming consumer + function call hooks)
- Week 3: implement redaction adapter & run initial evaluation on sample queries
- Week 4: report with precision lift, latency numbers, and recommended config (quantization/batching)

Action items (owners):
- Samira: confirm environment choice + send labeled query set (owner: CareLane)
- Ben: draft PoC technical runbook and SDK patch plan (owner: Ben Carter)
- Kimberly: prepare security checklist and required audit fields for redaction (owner: Kimberly Park)
- Mina: coordinate PoC timeline and internal sign-off (owner: Mina Haddad)

Attaching: carelane-discovery-notes.pdf (call notes + sample queries) and carelane-security-questions.xlsx (initial security checklist).

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Discovery — embed/rerank + streaming requirements

Samira — appreciate the clear asks. A few technical clarifications and an initial scope I will draft into the PoC runbook: 

Technical clarifications:
- Streaming + incremental scores: we can stream token-by-token for generation and emit per-candidate scores as they are produced. For rerank pipelines we typically run a lightweight embed->cosine step then pass top-N candidates to a reranker model that returns both final score and structured fields; we can stream those results as they complete.
- SDK changes: client will need a streaming consumer for partial score updates and an SDK hook to invoke local redaction before submission. I will attach a minimal SDK patch diff in the runbook.
- Latency constraints: to meet sub-300ms for short prompts we should target a small model + dedup cache on frequent prompts. We'll include batching knobs but default to single-request low-latency mode for clinical flows.

Proposed PoC checklist (technical):
1) Setup hybrid network flow: local redaction adapter -> Redwood staging rerank cluster
2) Implement SDK streaming consumer sample (JS + Python examples)
3) Run evaluation on labeled set (200–500 queries) and capture top-1/top-3 precision and the 95th percentile latency
4) Produce a short runbook with configuration suggestions (batch size, cache TTL, model quantization)

I'll push the initial runbook to the shared Drive by end of day and post a HubSpot note under deal CL-1342.

- Ben
VP, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
